environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 5000 m (16,404 ft)
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) normal operation
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics-qsfp28: 100 GbE or 40 GbE; channelizes to 4 x 25 GbE, 4 x 10 GbE or 2 x 50 GbE (guide Table 5)
features.virtual-chassis: up to 2 switches of the same model; any non-channelized QSFP28 port (0 to 31) can be a virtual chassis port, from 20.3R1

management.oob: one RJ-45 management port (MGMT) on the port side, with a link activity lamp

performance.qsfp28-port-31: 100, 40 or 2 x 50 GbE only, because its lanes are shared with the 10 GbE SFP+ port (Table 5)
performance.qsfp28-speeds: 100 or 40 GbE; ports 0 to 30 channelize to 4 x 25, 4 x 10 or 2 x 50 GbE

physical.depth-note: 20.27 in (51.5 cm) excluding the fan and power supply handles (Table 9)
physical.weight-note: 21.12 lb (9.58 kg) with two power supplies and six fan modules installed (Table 9)

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 6 A at 100 VAC and 3.8 A at 240 VAC
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40.8 to -72 VDC, 16 A maximum
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing and fully redundant; both should be installed

thermal.fans: six fan modules, 5+1; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

gaps.wanted: The depth ranges of the QFX5120-32C-RMK-E kit and the positions of its brackets. The guide describes the kit in prose and gives figures per step but no dimension; the library holds no kit contract for it.
What the light blue bar at the foot of the right-hand cluster is. The guide's text and its callouts do not name it.

The guide's Table 12 and figure 45 give the management port one lamp (link activity); the photograph shows two lamp windows (yellow and green) in the jack. One lamp is stated, as the guide has it, and the jack is the library's two-lamp Ethernet jack.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation. The tongue is blue in the photograph (qfx5120-32c-front-high.jpg), the kit's default skin.
The depth of the fan modules and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.

The guide (Tables 7, 23 and 26) says the 32C's back-to-front fan modules and supplies are lettered B2F with a blue handle. The reused QFX5200-48Y back-to-front fan module (QFX520048Y-FAN-AI) draws a chip lettered AIR IN, as that line's guide has it. The part number agrees and the chip is the part's, so it is not redrawn here; no photograph of a 32C back-to-front unit is held.

The fan numbers and lamps are printed on the grey plate to the left of the next fan module. A seated module's own flange paints over that plate, so the numerals are drawn on the chassis and hidden by a seated module in the explorer (lint L21, in the baseline), and each lamp names the two fans whose bays it touches so that it does not overlap a bay it does not serve.
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 8 bays (rear 8); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 9: 1.7 in (4.33 cm) high, 17.26 in (43.84 cm) wide, 20.27 in (51.5 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 21.12 lb (9.58 kg) with two supplies and the fans. The metric figures are carried: 4.33 cm is 43.3 mm where 1.7 in is 43.18, the table's own rounding. Unlike the 48T row the table gives the 32C no front-bracket width, so the body is the width and brackets are not modelled. The depth is the guide's 20.27 in, 8.5 mm shorter than the 48-port models' 20.48 in.

colour.note: The front plate samples #90908e (median of a bare patch under the jacks) and the rear end plates a darker grey; the chassis colour is the front's. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's four-post mounting for the 32C is the QFX5120-32C-RMK-E toolless rack mount kit (a pair of side mounting brackets, and a pair of front and rear rails), with a two-post mounting that uses the brackets (figures 89 to 95); the library holds no kit contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-cluster.note: At the right of the port side, 16.9 by 13.7 mm jack frames: MGMT above CON, centred 371.8 mm and 15.9 and 32.5 mm down (the MGMT label above and CON between), the SFP+ pair centred 389.7 mm, then the USB port, standing on end, 402.5 mm across and centred 15.5 mm down with its trident printed under it, and RUNNING JUNOS printed under it again. The MGMT frame shows two lamp windows at its top corners, yellow at the left and green at the right, though Table 12 and figure 45 name one lamp (link activity) and the jack is drawn as the library's two-lamp Ethernet jack, so one lamp is stated (green activity) and the other is left without a state. The USB tongue is blue in the photograph, the colour of a USB 3.0 port, and the kit's default skin is the blue one; the guide states no USB generation.

front-plate.note: At the left, a darker plate (21.1 to 44.3 mm) carries the maker's logo (not drawn: a logo-zone is reserved), the model name "QFX5120-32C", the chassis ID lamp and its legend "ID" at 41.4 mm across and the RESET legend with the pinhole at 38.4 mm across and 26.7 mm down. A light blue bar stands at the foot between the SFP+ pair and the end grid, 17.0 by 2.8 mm; the guide does not name it and it is drawn as decor and recorded as a gap.

gate-1.note: The front studio photograph is orthographic enough to measure: its body, between the left rim and the right edge, is 1823 px wide and about 179 px high (top edge row 130, bottom row 309), an aspect of 10.2 against the table's 438.4 / 43.3 = 10.12 (0.7 percent out, inside a pixel of edge placement). Scale 4.158 px/mm across and 4.13 down. The rear photograph reads 1794 x 176 px, 10.19, at 4.09 px/mm across and 4.065 down (its bounding box also catches the drop shadow, so the edges were read on a 3.6 times crop). The guide's own flat figures 19 and 20 are the same two pictures at 1500 px wide and agree with the photographs on every count and legend.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement on 2026-10-22. No Juniper notice was found and the guide states none. Third-party trackers list an announcement of 2021-01-20 and end of sale of 2021-10-04 for QFX5120-48Y part numbers only, and none for the 32C, so the device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX520048Y-FAN-AO and -AI, Table 23) and the power supplies (AC QFX520048Y-APSU-AO and -AI, Table 25; DC QFX520048Y-DPSU-AO and -AI, Table 35) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. THE LIBRARY ALREADY HOLDS EACH BY ITS PART NUMBER, as the QFX5200-48Y's parts (juniper/qfx5200-48y-fan-afo@1, -afi@1, -apsu-ao@1, -apsu-ai@1, -dpsu-ao@1, -dpsu-ai@1), so they are reused as they are and none is added. The guide spells the fan "QFX520048Y-FAN-AO" here as the QFX5200 guide does. The face of those modules is the QFX5200-48Y's photograph (the same maker, part number, red latch and F2B chip); whether the 32C's units are the identical hardware cannot be settled from the documents held, so the pairing is by part number as the brief requires. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. The guide says to fit a blank cover over an empty supply slot but names no part number for it, so no blank is modelled and no empty-bay configuration is offered. The guide lists no -S variant.

port-lamps.note: Each QSFP28 port has four lamps (guide Table 15: the first for the unchannelized link, the other three for the channels of a channelized port), in a row above the upper cage and below the lower one, centred at 3.4, 7.5, 11.7 and 15.8 mm from the cell's left edge and 3.5 mm above the upper cell and 13.3 mm below the lower cell's top (read at 4 times and good to 0.25 mm). Each SFP+ port has one lamp (Table 14); both sit above the pair, at x 387.0 and 393.3 mm and y 9.7 mm, with the up and down arrows between them. The lamps are unlit light pipes in the photograph, which resolves them as faint rings, so their colours are the guide's table (green), not read off the picture. Table 15 gives green steady and blinking only; the beacon behaviour the 48Y table adds is not stated for the 32C, so none is written.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 19: the QSFP28 ports run 0 to 31 down each column, even above the cage and odd below it, each numeral centred over or under its cage, with the four lamps beside it. The SFP+ ports are 32 above 33: the photograph prints "32 (lamp) up-arrow down-arrow (lamp) 33" on one line above the pair. Interface names are not printed and the guide held does not state them; none is written here.

ports.note: Front photograph, dark cage openings across the upper row: 16 columns of 77 px (18.5 mm) openings on a pitch of 79 px, which is 19.0 mm, the registry's QSFP28 ganged pitch, in four blocks of four columns. The first openings start at 318, 649, 980 and 1312 px, so the cells start at 46.2, 125.8, 205.4 and 285.3 mm, a stride of 79.7 mm and a gutter of 79.7 - 4 x 19.0 = 3.7 mm. Counts are 32 and 2, the guide's callouts 1 and 3 of figure 21. The cells use the registry's aperture (18.5 x 9.58).

power.note: Table 27 (AC supplies): 173 W typical, 365 W maximum, input 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 6 A at 100 VAC and 3.8 A at 240 VAC; the maximum assumes 3.5 W for each 100G optical module. Table 37 (DC supplies): 231 W typical, 493 W maximum, 16 A maximum, rated -48 to 60 VDC, operating range -40.8 to 72 VDC, with the same 3.5 W note. The two tables carry different figures for the same box and the guide states no ambient for either, so both are kept and the AC pair is filed as the device's, since AC is the default build.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.09 px/mm, checked against guide figure 20 and callouts 1 to 3 of figures 22 and 23. Supply slot PS0 is at the left end and PS1 at the right end, each with a block arrow, its PS legend, an earth symbol and an earthing screw on the end plate (15.6 mm and 17.0 mm wide). Between them six fan modules sit on a 48.6 mm pitch: each module is a grey flange with a captive screw at its left (8.3 mm, the width the QFX5200 guide's flat figure gives for the same part) and the grille. The number of fan n and its round lamp are printed on the flange of the module to its right (and for fan 5 on a plain strip with two screws before PS1), the lamp carrying an arrow pointing back at the fan it serves. The screws read at 72.3 mm + 48.6 n.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: Figure 20 and the photograph agree, and both show the front-to-back (F2B) build, red handles and red ejector levers: it is the default configuration. Table 7 and Table 26 settle the colours: red and F2B for front-to-back, blue and B2F for back-to-front (the 48-port models say AIR OUT and AIR IN with Juniper Gold and Juniper Azure Blue instead).

row-pitch.note: Down the first cage column the openings are 187 to 226 px and 239 to 278 px, centres 206.5 and 258.5 px, which are 18.4 and 30.9 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 12.5 mm. The two SFP+ cages and the two RJ-45 jacks at the right share that grid (the SFP+ frames read 182.5 to 225.5 px and 234.5 to 277 px, a pitch of 12.4 mm, and are 10.3 mm high against the registry's 10.4). y is good to about 0.25 mm.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5120 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-09-30, 339 pages (copyright Hewlett Packard Enterprise Development LP; the PDF states no terms of use beyond the copyright notice, and a reference copy is kept outside the repository), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5120/qfx5120.pdf: the front and rear figures 19 to 23 (the flat views are g100345 and g100346), Table 4 (release and features), Table 5 (channelization), Table 6 (Virtual Chassis), Table 7 (models and variants), Table 9 (physical specifications), Tables 10, 12, 14 and 15 (the lamps), Tables 22 to 26 (fan modules and AC supplies), Tables 27, 35 to 37 (power and the DC supplies) and Table 50 (environment). Juniper's studio photographs of the 32C, front and rear, 2100 x 443 and 2100 x 417 px (image library, www.juniper.net/ content/dam/www/assets/images/us/en/image-library/qfx-series/qfx5120-32c/ qfx5120-32c-front-high.jpg and -rear-high.jpg; no terms of use are stated on the files, and nothing of either is copied here, since every skin is drawn new from measurements). THE QFX5120 ETHERNET SWITCH DATASHEET (juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/qfx5120-ethernet-switch-datasheet.pdf) DID NOT ANSWER: both attempts to fetch it timed out with no bytes received, so no datasheet figure is used and every figure here is the guide's or is read off a photograph. No mechanical drawing, Visio stencil or 3D model was found for the QFX5120-32C. The intake folders held for the Juniper EX and QFX lines were not readable from the host this was built on (permission denied), so none could be looked in.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the light latch tongues at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention, here read off the device for the QSFP28 rows and the SFP+ pair.

vents.note: One band of hexagonal holes along the top edge from 42.1 to 406.9 mm (two staggered rows, 5.0 mm apart along a row), a row of slots along the foot from 37.1 mm, and a grid of 3.9 mm square holes at each end (three columns on a 5.05 mm pitch and eight rows on 4.95 mm, 7.0 to 22.2 mm and 417.7 to 433.0 mm). Each is drawn as a vent strip on the pitch read at 4 times, estimated: the hexagons are a rectangular approximation of a hexagon field, and the fourth column the photograph shows in the last two rows at the left is not drawn.
